## TL;DR

I ran a QA pass on the Deployments and Context pages against fixtures only, at 375, 768 and 1280 px, and fixed what it found. Failed deploys, failed loads, empty repos and very long names and logs were each checked. The main problems were long names that pushed controls off-screen, raw error text with no next step, and an unstyled load-error element. The cases are now covered by a browser QA test (36 cases) and a helper unit test (8 cases). The QA record is in `docs/qa/2026-11-deployments-context-qa.md`. Nothing ran on a real device, a live server, a real provider or a git remote.

## Work and rationale

I followed the Agents QA pattern already in the repo: mount the real view in jsdom with a stubbed `fetch`, then render the captured markup in headless WebKit with the built global stylesheet and the view's compiled scoped CSS. Each case asserts that no element leaves the viewport and that no box clips its own text sideways.

The first baseline run caught a harness problem before any product bug. Playwright's `textContent` waited 30 seconds for hint elements that did not exist yet, so the harness now reports a missing element straight away. The Context view reads docs from a store that `App.vue` primes at startup, so the harness primes it too before mounting.

Product changes:

- **Deployments.** Wrapping for the `ff from` pill, the Deploy button label, service and provider names and env errors. The `.dep-err` load-error class had no CSS, so it now has styles and a "Press Refresh to try again" line. A configured repo with no targets shows a plain empty panel instead of an empty matrix.
- **Refused push.** `deployFailureHint()` in `src/ui-app/src/lib/deployment-failure.ts` maps the git output to a cause and a next step. The raw output moves into a box that scrolls on its own, in both the dialog and the outcome panel. The copy says "different commits" rather than "diverged" and states that RepoOS never force-pushes.
- **Context.** The tab row wraps, which fixes the Refresh button leaving the viewport at 375 px and a 38 px sideways clip of `.ctx-page`. Doc and skill names, the doc title and the path wrap. The doc body says what went wrong and what to do instead of `(could not load)`. The empty docs state says where to add a file, and the Skills.sh error gained a "Try again" line.

No config keys or task formats changed.

## Approaches tried

The overflow audit went through three versions. Exempting every scroller passed everything and hid the 1280 px clips. Asserting only the viewport also missed them. The version that works asserts both: no element outside the viewport, and no unexpected sideways clipping, with `pre` and `.md-table-wrap` exempt, since both are built to scroll.

For the refused-push output I considered a collapsed `<details>`. I rejected it because the raw git text is the evidence a user needs when the hint is not enough, so it stays visible in a box with a height cap.

In the refused-push case the first Deploy button was disabled, because `main` has an environment error. That is correct behaviour, so the harness now clicks the first enabled button.

## Challenges and blockers

Verification is fixture-driven and headless WebKit at three widths. A real refused push, a real Skills.sh outage and a real phone or tablet have not been reproduced. The QA doc says so.

The full-page screenshot at 375 px shows the refused-push dialog's header above the top of the frame. The capture is of a fixed overlay, so this may be an artefact of the full-page capture, but I did not confirm it in a real viewport. A human should check that dialog on a phone before this is treated as closed.

The first handoff was refused. The remote run failed `tests/checks-releases-data-responsive.test.ts` at 375 px on the thinkpad runner, with no assertion detail in the message. That test is not one I changed, and it passed locally alone and alongside the two Deployments/Context suites. I could not reproduce the exact assertion. The likely cause is the test's own polls: three `expect.poll` calls used Vitest's 1 s default timeout while the fixture's responses are deliberately delayed. I gave those polls the page's 5 s budget. This is a hardening change, not a proven root cause. If the remote run fails again, the next step is to read its assertion output.

`repoos check` ran scoped with `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main`. Locally I ran the new QA file, the helper test and the related existing suites. I did not run the full unscoped suite.

## Key learnings

An overflow check with an exemption list needs its exemptions reviewed. A scroller excuse looked reasonable and hid the most visible class of bug on the page. Asserting that content is contained, not merely scrollable, is the stronger check.

A failure message is only half the fix. Each raw server string needs a plain-English cause and a next step, with the raw text kept in a bounded box so the reader still has the evidence. The helper's table test keeps the copy honest as the server's messages change.

When a page's data comes from a store primed at app startup, a view-level test has to prime that store the same way. Otherwise it reports an empty page and looks like it passed.
